Natural Resources Canada, Canadian Industry Program for Energy Conservation (CIPEC), and the Mining Association of Canada (2005). Benchmarking the Energy Consumption of Canadian Underground Bulk Mines. Ottawa: NRCan Office of Energy Efficiency. ISBN 0-662-39539-5; Cat. No. M144-71/2005E. Authors and consultant not named on the title page or imprint (international comparison by Competitive Analysis Centre Inc. (CACI) with AME Mineral Economics).

Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 6). Survey of 11 Canadian underground bulk mines (base metals and gold; 10 with above-ground detail: 5 gold recovery plants, 5 base-metals concentrators), MAC members. The report prints for every stage only the HIGH : LOW range across the sample (energy in kWhe per t ore hoisted for mining, per t ore milled for mills); no mean or median, and per-mine bars are chart labels (not loaded, mine identities are anonymous). Loaded: all stage ranges as specific-energy-consumption with value blank and min/max. Zero minima are as printed and mean a plant does not report that stage (crushing underground, gravity, tailings, mill support). kWhe converts every carrier (including explosives at 1.06 kWhe/kg) to one number, so the carrier split is unknown; target total used. NOT supplied: mine-air heating (no separate figure; heating appears only as mill heating and lighting) so direct-heater_mine-air-* stay unfilled; no costs of equipment (energy costs only, in other-values). Source inconsistencies: Sect. 4 vs Sect. 5 cost ranges differ slightly (see other-values). The data year is not stated; international comparison year is 1999. No TRL or capex.
